parts.note: a senior ward nurse is called Sister in Britain, and the same post held by a man needs a sex-neutral title

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a brother who is called Sister.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals 'Sister' is the title of the nurse running a ward; a man in that post takes the neutral title instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The nurse in charge of a ward, once always called Sister, has a gender-neutral job title.

indicators.note: made good as in reformed or put right, so the letters of RAF aces are reworked

explanation.surface: Air force pilots became fine bearers of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Carafes are glass jugs used to hold and pour water or wine at table.

clue.text: Former Loire province recorded in Roman journals

indicators.note: the answer is written down inside the words Roman journals

explanation.surface: An old French region gets a mention in ancient Roman writings.
explanation.definitionFit: Anjou was a historic province of France in the Loire valley, around Angers.

clue.text: Feature of the Cheshire cat swallowing a milk-shake-the old moggy!

indicators.note: the cat's feature takes another piece down inside it

parts.note: the Cheshire cat in Alice in Wonderland is famous for its grin

indicators.note: a shake mixes things up, so the letters of a milk are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Cheshire cat's grin as it drinks a milk shake, an old pussy cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk-shake' reads as the drink, but 'shake' is the anagram signal on A MILK. Moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimalkin is an archaic name for an old cat, especially a female one.

clue.text: Knotted fibres of animal on its back

indicators.note: an animal lying on its back is upside down, so in a down clue the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lion is an animal, the big cat

explanation.surface: Tangled hair of an animal lying on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short knotted fibre combed out of wool or silk before spinning.

parts.note: not scrapping the old gold coin but killing the monarch

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the pound coin called a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin worth a pound, which leads the surface astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicide is the killing of a king or queen.

parts.note: not a winner at the children's game but the Scottish earl who championed and removed the Parthenon sculptures

explanation.surface: The best marbles player in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Elgin Marbles, sculptures from the Parthenon, were taken to Britain by a Scottish earl whose title is also a town in Moray.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish earl who brought the Parthenon sculptures to London gave them his title.

clue.text: They go to sea, we hear, and retain their colour on board

indicators.note: we hear signals the spoken phrase is the one to be written down

parts.note: people go to sea by ships

explanation.surface: Sailors go to sea and keep their flag flying on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By ships', how people go to sea, sounds like the chess pieces; a chess bishop stays on squares of one colour all game.
explanation.definitionFit: Each chess bishop moves diagonally and so is confined to squares of a single colour on the chessboard.

clue.text: Hoopla, for example, legitimate object for attack

definitions.meaning: hoopla is a fairground game of throwing rings over prizes
someone it is acceptable to criticise or target

explanation.definitionFit: Hoopla is a sideshow at a funfair, and the idiom describes anyone open to legitimate criticism.

clue.text: Regarding little woman finishing of the cake and celebrating

parts.note: re is a short word meaning regarding or about
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women
icing is what finishes off a cake on top

explanation.surface: Someone talks about a small woman putting the last touch to a cake for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' points to Jo, one of the four March sisters in the novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Rejoicing and celebrating both mean showing great gladness at good news.

definitions.meaning: to peach is old slang for to inform on someone to the police

explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang: an informer peaches on mates, and cannabis has many street names including weed.

indicators.note: the word Gaul is wrecked and its letters rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Tight-fisted French ruin the ancient land of Gaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparing and frugal both describe someone careful not to spend or waste much.

clue.text: Arsenic administered with love-that is the summary of the plot

indicators.note: arsenic administered is dosed out, so the word arsenic is reworked into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A poisoner gives arsenic with affection: that is the gist of the murder story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link joining wordplay to definition; in tennis scoring 'love' means zero, written as O.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a film or play.

clue.text: Funnels of steamship taking in new course

indicators.note: the steamship abbreviation takes another piece inside it

parts.note: a tack is a new course taken by a sailing ship

explanation.surface: A steamer with smoking funnels changes direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's funnels are its smokestacks, also simply called stacks.

clue.text: Constable, perhaps, on track of great talent

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed on top of the next piece

parts.note: John Constable was a famous English painter, an example of an artist
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A policeman walking his beat shows a great gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' suggests a policeman but is the landscape painter John Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistry is creative skill, great talent in an art.

clue.text: The only way to have a word in with Gabby!

definitions.text: The only way to have a word in with Gabby!

parts.words: The only way to have a word in with Gabby!
parts.note: with a chatterbox you can only squeeze a word in sideways, as the idiom about getting a word in puts it

explanation.surface: A complaint about a friend called Gabby who never lets anyone speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'get a word in edgeways', said of a talker who leaves no gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of squeezing a remark in sideways against a nonstop talker uses this word.

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters of women tend are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women are inclined to switch their insurance plans.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a kind of life insurance policy paying out at a fixed date.

clue.text: Way to serve potatoes-just surrounding game

indicators.note: the word for just goes round another piece

parts.note: due as in fair and deserved, a just reward
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A recipe for potatoes, served around some meat from the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests pheasant or venison with the potatoes, but it is the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are mashed with egg and piped into rosettes before baking.

indicators.note: culture as in cultivation, working the ground over, signals the words Latin sub are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A city known for its Latin sub-culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub-culture' reads as one word, but 'sub' is fodder and 'culture' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is the great Turkish city on the Bosphorus.

clue.text: Clumsily, paint spilled over ends of laundry

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the following piece
paint spilled is scattered, so its letters are rearranged
the first and last letters of the word laundry are taken

explanation.surface: Paint is clumsily knocked over on to the washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaptly means in an awkward, unsuitable or unskilful way.

parts.note: a notice in a paper whose name is itself a shortened form of a longer word

explanation.surface: A complaint about being told something at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short notice' usually means little warning, but here it is a public notice whose name is a clipped word.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a published notice, and its name is a clipping of the longer advertisement.

clue.text: In new jersey, we hear, split is in fashion

indicators.note: the word for split goes inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style, as in high society
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: A torn new sweater is still stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jersey' suggests a sweater, but it is the US state: one hears of this as the place in New Jersey, its state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenton is the state capital of New Jersey in the United States.

parts.note: jack is a sailor, an AB or able seaman, so jack's is AB's
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack is drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' (jack tar) is a crossword sailor, as is AB, an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green wormwood-flavoured spirit.

explanation.surface: Something written down becomes famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both written down and well known or eminent.

indicators.note: ready as in made ready, prepared, signals the letters of wheat's are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The crop is ripe for cutting with a scythe.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's gives its S here: the six letters W H E A T S rearrange, and the whole clue describes the cut crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A swathe is the strip of grain or grass cut by one sweep of a scythe.

indicators.note: the opening letters of the opera title are taken as the answer

explanation.surface: The opening theme of Wagner's opera The Mastersingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mastersingers of Nuremberg is a Wagner opera; the word is the German and Latin for a musical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Thema is the term for a theme or subject, especially in music or argument.

definitions.meaning: to husband resources is to use them sparingly

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to keep something back rather than spend it; husbanding is careful economy.

clue.text: Pack of cards worth a fortune?

definitions.text: Pack of cards worth a fortune?

parts.words: Pack of cards worth a fortune?
parts.note: not a valuable deck but one used to tell a fortune

explanation.surface: A deck of playing cards that is extremely valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worth a fortune' suggests great value; the fortune is the one a reader foretells.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarot cards are a special deck used by fortune-tellers to divine the future.

parts.note: a teller works at a bank, but a teller is also someone who tells, whose words are a declaration

explanation.surface: A bank clerk draws up a customer's account.
explanation.walkthrough: A bank sends a written account of your money, and a 'teller' read literally is one who tells, producing a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank's printed summary of an account and a spoken declaration share one name.

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of residential are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loud locomotive disturbs the people living nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' is a link meaning the letters of the word 'residential'.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive powered by an oil-burning compression-ignition motor is this kind of engine.
